chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid and Ibn Abi Umayr together, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara and others besides these two, from one of the two (peace be upon them both) regarding
the wergild. He said: 'It is one hundred camels, and there are neither dinars in it, nor dirhams, nor anything other than that.'

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Diya (wergild/blood money): compensatory payment due to the family of a victim of killing or bodily harm
key_terms.الْإِبِلُ: Ibil (camels): the specific commodity designated as the diya in this ruling
key_terms.دَرَاهِمُ: Darahim (dirhams): silver coins, also explicitly excluded
key_terms.دَنَانِيرُ: Dananir (dinars): gold coins, explicitly excluded as a valid diya payment

ai.seo_question: What is the form of diya (blood money) in Shia Islamic law according to Imam al-Baqir or al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes that the diya (blood money/wergild) for intentional or erroneous killing is specifically one hundred camels — not gold dinars, silver dirhams, or any other form of payment. The ruling comes through a chain of highly trusted companions who narrated from either Imam al-Baqir or Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon them). In classical Islamic jurisprudence, different schools debated the acceptable forms of diya payment; this narration represents the Shia position that camels are the primary and original form.
